course.eras.broom.chapter.desc: The sweep arm passes over a whole run of cells, so the number of ways in is no longer fixed.
course.eras.broom.chapter.title: Many ways in
course.eras.paper.chapter.desc: Build the answer to a big problem out of the answers to small ones.
course.eras.paper.chapter.title: Pen and paper
course.eras.ranger.chapter.desc: It sees further, two cells away; it sees more, the two words a table compares; and it can scan the other way round.
course.eras.ranger.chapter.title: Seeing further
course.eras.reach.chapter.desc: A telescopic arm reaches a cell however far away.
course.eras.reach.chapter.title: A longer arm
course.eras.scout.chapter.desc: On every cell the robot runs the same circuit board, and a finished board becomes a component.
course.eras.scout.chapter.title: Build a machine
course.eras.settle.chapter.desc: When the arrows loop round, scan again and again.
course.eras.settle.chapter.title: Scan until it settles
course.eras.stack.chapter.desc: When one number can’t remember enough, remember one more thing.
course.eras.stack.chapter.title: When the state falls short
course.lede: No programming or algorithms background needed. Starting from counting routes by hand, you learn to break a big problem into a table and fill it in cell by cell; in the end you wire up the circuit boards that count routes, compare words and pack a backpack, and see why they are so fast.
course.title: State Graph
